key_insight: The paper generalizes thermodynamic dislocation theory to arbitrary uniform stress and strain states, showing that macroscopic plastic flow emerges as an associated J2 theory with hardening governed by dislocation kinetics rather than empirical fitting.
engineering_relevance: It provides a single physics-based constitutive framework that can predict tension, compression, and torsion of copper across wide temperature and strain-rate ranges using one parameter set.
method: Extend orientation averaging from axial loading to general macroscopic stress/strain states using equal-probability grain orientations.
Use root-mean-square averages of resolved shear stress and shear strains over slip-system orientations.
Couple the averaged flow rule to thermally activated dislocation depinning, dislocation density evolution, and effective disorder temperature evolution in time rate form.
evidence_signal: The model was calibrated on Hopkinson-bar tension, dynamic compression, and torque-twist data, and one parameter set matched 142 data points within about 6% rms over 10 to 2300 s^-1 and room temperature to 1173 K.
watch_item: The framework depends on the assumed initial dislocation state and equal-orientation averaging, so specimen history and texture effects may need careful treatment in new materials or loading paths.
paper_title: Averaging in thermodynamic dislocation theory: general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states
